meta.description: Quantifies CRISPR editing outcomes with CRISPResso2 across Cas9-nuclease (indels, HDR), CBE/ABE base editors, and prime editor modes; covers single-amplicon, batch, pooled, WGS off-target, and comparison workflows plus quantification-window math and failure-mode diagnosis.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated statistics, DOIs, or trial results found across any of the 7 outputs; all reported percentages trace to real CRISPResso2 runs or the upstream expected-results files.

practice_boundaries.detail: Research-scope amplicon quantification only; no diagnostic or prescriptive claims about a person or patient.

methodological_ground.detail: Quantification-window sizing and the substitution-vs-indel diagnostic are methodologically sound and were independently confirmed to give the correct call on a known-Cas9 sample.

code_usability.detail: The Skill's own 'Parse Output in Python' function (parse_crispresso) was run verbatim against real CRISPResso2 output and crashed with ValueError: too many values to unpack -- it assumes CRISPResso_mapping_statistics.txt is one key\tvalue pair per line, but the real file is a 7-column, 2-row TSV. The code also reads a READS_ALIGNED_PERCENTAGE key that does not exist in that file at all, contradicting the Skill's own 'no percentage columns' note for that same file (Input 6).

functional_suitability.note: Covers all 5 CRISPResso2 modes plus HDR/CBE/ABE/PE variants (Completeness 4/4). Correctness docked to 2/4: the bundled Python parsing snippet crashes on real output and CRISPRessoPooled's default read-count threshold is undocumented -- both confirmed by execution, not inferred.

reliability.note: The single-amplicon Cas9 failure-mode table is strong, but the CRISPRessoPooled all-NA-on-small-pool failure and the broken parsing snippet are neither caught, warned about, nor surfaced anywhere in SKILL.md or usage-guide.md.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md ~360 lines with usage-guide.md and examples/ split out; reasonable disclosure with minor duplication between the two docs' mode cheat-sheets.

agent_usability.note: Mode decision tree and output-file tables are clear and internally consistent for the Cas9 path. Error Prevention docked for missing the pooled-mode min-reads trap, the broken parse snippet, and a direct contradiction between the mapping-stats output table and the Python example on the same page.

human_usability.note: Natural researcher-phrased trigger examples throughout usage-guide.md; the underlying CLI fails loudly and clearly on badly mismatched input (verified), which is the correct behavior for this domain, not a usability defect.

security.note: No hardcoded secrets or injection vectors; all user input is sequence strings and file paths passed as CLI arguments. Minor: no mention of handling patient-derived-sample sensitivity if this Skill is ever pointed at clinical amplicon data.

maintainability.note: Clean SKILL.md/usage-guide.md/examples split (Modularity 4/4). Testability docked hard: the one bundled Python code sample is untested and fails immediately when actually run against real CRISPResso2 output.

agent_specific.note: Strong, precise triggering; correct progressive-disclosure layering; explicit, clean Related-Skills composability with base-editing-analysis, prime-editing-screens, and library-design. Escape Hatches docked slightly for no explicit human-handoff guidance beyond the Mode Decision Tree's failure list.

inputs.label: Single Cas9 amplicon indel quantification (FANCF locus)
inputs.note: CRISPResso 2.3.4 (Docker) on FANC.Cas9.fastq: without --min_average_read_quality 30 reproduced upstream's 26.38297872% Modified byte-for-byte (235/250 aligned). With the flag, exactly as the Skill's own worked example specifies, got 24.88687783% Modified (221/250 aligned) -- a real, undocumented shift from the recommended default.

assertions.text: Output reports % unmodified vs % NHEJ/modified for the amplicon
assertions.note: CRISPResso_quantification_of_editing_frequency.txt has Unmodified%/Modified% columns as documented.

assertions.text: Skill flags whether editing efficiency meets the >70% functional-KO threshold
assertions.note: Quantitative Thresholds table gives this exact threshold and rationale.

assertions.text: The Skill's own worked example (with --min_average_read_quality 30) reproduces the same editing % as CRISPResso2's published expected result for this exact test amplicon
assertions.note: Got 24.89% with the recommended flag vs. the upstream/no-filter 26.38%; the Skill never notes that this flag changes the number.

assertions.text: Mapping-statistics file structure matches what SKILL.md's own output table describes
assertions.note: Verified: 7 space-named columns, one data row, no percentage columns -- exactly as documented.

inputs.label: CBE base-editor quantification-window code path
inputs.note: CRISPResso --base_editor_output --conversion_nuc_from C --conversion_nuc_to T -w 10 -wc -10 on FANC.Cas9.fastq produced real per-position C/T percentages (~95-97% wild-type C at every target position). Indel-dominated modification pattern correctly flags as non-clean-BE via the Skill's own substitution-vs-indel ratio, matching this sample's true Cas9 origin.

assertions.text: Per-position C-to-T conversion % table is produced and parses
assertions.note: Quantification_window_nucleotide_percentage_table.txt has real, non-zero A/C/G/T/- rows per position.

assertions.text: Skill's substitution-vs-indel ratio diagnostic correctly identifies this as Cas9-like (not clean BE) given the sample's known true origin
assertions.note: Indels (49 del + 8 ins) dominate substitutions (7); ratio is well under the Skill's <3 Cas9-like threshold.

assertions.text: Skill explicitly requires specifying --conversion_nuc_from/--conversion_nuc_to for correct BE chemistry
assertions.note: Documented, and confirmed against the CLI's actual default.

assertions.text: Bystander rate reported separately from target rate as the Skill instructs
assertions.note: Per-position table structure supports separating target vs. bystander positions.

inputs.label: Low-alignment / wrong-amplicon diagnostic
inputs.note: Two runs: a 3'-truncated amplicon still aligned 220/250 reads (reads too short to reach the truncated region, doesn't reproduce a low-alignment symptom); FANC reads run against the HEK3 amplicon+guide instead crashed hard -- CRITICAL: Alignment error, No alignments were found, exit 1, no output folder at all.

assertions.text: Skill's failure-mode table helps diagnose a real low/zero-alignment run
assertions.note: Table only describes the graded '<50% but present' case, not the total-failure crash-with-no-output case actually observed.

assertions.text: Documented fix path (re-derive amplicon boundaries, check strand) is actionable
assertions.note: Generic guidance still correctly applies to the wrong-amplicon scenario.

assertions.text: No misleading claim that misalignment always yields a graded percentage to inspect
assertions.note: Skill's diagnostic table implicitly assumes an output file with a percentage exists; a badly wrong amplicon instead crashes with none.

assertions.text: Diagnostic reasoning doesn't fabricate a root cause
assertions.note: CRITICAL error message from the tool itself is the evidence, not an invented explanation.

inputs.label: 2-amplicon arrayed validation pool (CRISPRessoPooled)
inputs.note: CRISPRessoPooled on Both.Cas9.fastq + Cas9.amplicons.txt (242-250 reads/amplicon), exactly as documented: exit 0, but SAMPLES_QUANTIFICATION_SUMMARY.txt has every field NA. Running log shows 'Skipping amplicon [FANC] because too few reads (242) align to it' against the undocumented default --min_reads_to_use_region 1000. Re-run with --min_reads_to_use_region 100 reproduced FANC 26.38297872% / HEK3 34.42622951%, matching upstream expected values exactly.

assertions.text: CRISPRessoPooled quickstart command, as documented, produces usable per-amplicon editing percentages on a realistic small pilot pool
assertions.note: All fields NA at default settings on this 242-250-read-per-amplicon pool.

assertions.note: Not mentioned anywhere in SKILL.md or usage-guide.md, despite being the exact parameter that silently breaks the Skill's own 'arrayed validation pool' example use case.

assertions.text: Once the threshold is corrected, demultiplexing assigns reads to the correct amplicon (no misassignment)

key_strengths: All CLI flags across five CRISPResso2 modes (CRISPResso, CRISPRessoBatch, CRISPRessoPooled, CRISPRessoWGS, CRISPRessoCompare) verified byte-accurate against the installed v2.3.4 CLI --help output.

Quantification-window math and the substitution-vs-indel diagnostic are correct: independently confirmed the ratio heuristic correctly identifies this audit's ground-truth Cas9 sample as non-BE when run through the base-editor code path.
CRISPRessoBatch reproduces the exact same per-sample editing percentage as a standalone CRISPResso run on the same sample (26.38297872%), confirming deterministic, idempotent behavior across modes.
Failure-mode documentation for the single-amplicon Cas9 path (low alignment, substitution inflation, bystander inflation, MMEJ) is detailed and, where tested, accurate.

recommendations.title: parse_crispresso() crashes on real CRISPResso output
recommendations.problem: The Skill's only bundled Python code sample raises ValueError: too many values to unpack on the first line of CRISPResso_mapping_statistics.txt, and separately reads a READS_ALIGNED_PERCENTAGE column that does not exist in that file.
recommendations.root_cause: The parser assumes one key\tvalue pair per line, but the real file is a 7-column, 2-row TSV (header + one data row) -- and the Skill's own 'Key outputs' table on the same page already says this file has 'no percentage columns', directly contradicting the code beneath it.
recommendations.fix: Rewrite parse_crispresso() to read the file with csv.DictReader or pandas.read_csv(sep='\t') and compute mapping_pct as READS_ALIGNED / READS_IN_INPUTS * 100 (or pull a percentage straight from CRISPResso2_info.json), then verify the rewritten snippet against a real output directory before shipping.

recommendations.title: CRISPRessoPooled silently returns all-NA on realistic pilot-scale pools
recommendations.problem: Running CRISPRessoPooled exactly as documented on a 2-amplicon, ~250-reads-per-amplicon pool -- the Skill's own canonical 'arrayed validation pool' use case -- produces a SAMPLES_QUANTIFICATION_SUMMARY.txt with every field NA, at exit code 0.
recommendations.root_cause: CRISPRessoPooled's default --min_reads_to_use_region is 1000; any amplicon below that is silently skipped. Neither SKILL.md nor usage-guide.md mentions this flag anywhere.
recommendations.fix: Document --min_reads_to_use_region in the Pooled-Amplicon Mode section with guidance to set it below the expected per-amplicon read depth for pilot/validation-scale pools, and add an explicit 'check for NA rows in SAMPLES_QUANTIFICATION_SUMMARY.txt' step to the What-the-Agent-Will-Do checklist.

recommendations.title: Recommended quality flag changes results without disclosure
recommendations.problem: The Single-Amplicon Cas9 worked example includes --min_average_read_quality 30; on the real test amplicon this drops aligned reads from 235 to 221 and shifts Modified% from 26.38% to 24.89%, with no note that this happens.
recommendations.root_cause: The example presents the quality filter as a neutral best-practice default without showing its numeric effect or telling the agent to check how many reads it discards.
recommendations.fix: Add a line noting that --min_average_read_quality changes the reported editing percentage, and instruct the agent to report the aligned-read fraction retained after filtering alongside the editing percentage.

recommendations.title: Low-alignment failure mode doesn't cover the total-failure case
recommendations.problem: When the amplicon is badly wrong (different locus), CRISPResso exits 1 with a CRITICAL error and writes no output folder at all -- but the Skill's Failure Modes table only describes a graded '<50% aligned' symptom with a percentage to inspect.
recommendations.root_cause: The documented diagnostic assumes an output file always exists to read a percentage from.
recommendations.fix: Add a row to Failure Modes for the hard-crash case ('CRITICAL: Alignment error, No alignments were found, exit 1, no output folder') alongside the existing graded low-alignment row.

recommendations.title: Mapping-stats output table contradicts the Python example on the same page
recommendations.problem: The 'Key outputs' table states CRISPResso_mapping_statistics.txt has 'no percentage columns', but the very next section's Python snippet reads a percentage column from that same file.
recommendations.root_cause: The two sections were not cross-checked against each other or against a real output file when written.
recommendations.fix: Correct one side to match the real file structure (confirmed: 7 space-named columns, one data row, no percentage column) so the two sections agree.
